update_log: Complete exhaustive baseline of high-frequency National Parks, focusing on flagship species, superlatives, and state locations for Geography Static GK.

national_parks.name: Hemis National Park
national_parks.key_fact: The largest national park in India; globally famous for having the highest density of snow leopards in any protected area.

national_parks.name: South Button Island National Park
national_parks.key_fact: The smallest national park in India (only 0.03 sq km).

national_parks.name: Jim Corbett National Park
national_parks.key_fact: The oldest national park in India (established in 1936 as Hailey National Park); first park to come under the Project Tiger initiative.

national_parks.name: Kaziranga National Park
national_parks.key_fact: UNESCO World Heritage Site; holds two-thirds of the world's Great One-horned Rhinoceros population.

national_parks.name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
national_parks.key_fact: The only floating national park in the world, located on Loktak Lake; characterized by floating decomposed plant material called 'phumdis'.

national_parks.name: Gir National Park
national_parks.key_fact: The only place in the world where Asiatic lions are found in the wild.

national_parks.name: Kuno National Park
national_parks.key_fact: Selected for the historic Cheetah Reintroduction Project in 2022; animals were brought from Namibia and South Africa.

national_parks.name: Namdapha National Park
national_parks.flagship_species: Namdapha Flying Squirrel, Snow Leopard, Clouded Leopard
national_parks.key_fact: The only park in the world to harbor all four feline species of big cat (Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Clouded Leopard).

national_parks.name: Bhitarkanika National Park
national_parks.key_fact: India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem; famous for mass nesting of Olive Ridley turtles at nearby Gahirmatha Beach.

national_parks.name: Sundarbans National Park
national_parks.key_fact: UNESCO World Heritage Site; largest mangrove forest in the world, heavily intersected by tidal waterways, mudflats, and small islands of salt-tolerant mangrove forests.

national_parks.name: Silent Valley National Park
national_parks.key_fact: Located in the Nilgiri Hills; famous for the 'Save Silent Valley' environmental movement in the 1970s.

national_parks.name: Periyar National Park
national_parks.key_fact: Located high in the Cardamom Hills; unique because boat safaris on Periyar Lake are the primary way to view wildlife.

national_parks.name: Bandipur National Park
national_parks.key_fact: Part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve; shares its boundaries with Nagarhole, Mudumalai, and Wayanad.

national_parks.name: Ranthambore National Park
national_parks.key_fact: Famous for its diurnal tigers (active during the day) and the historic 10th-century Ranthambore Fort within the park.

national_parks.name: Desert National Park
national_parks.key_fact: One of the largest national parks in India; an excellent example of the ecosystem of the Thar Desert.

national_parks.name: Kanha National Park
national_parks.key_fact: The largest national park in Madhya Pradesh; famously inspired Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book'.

national_parks.name: Manas National Park
national_parks.flagship_species: Pygmy Hog, Golden Langur, Wild Water Buffalo
national_parks.key_fact: A UNESCO Natural World Heritage site, a Project Tiger reserve, an elephant reserve, and a biosphere reserve.

national_parks.name: Khangchendzonga National Park
national_parks.key_fact: India's first and only 'Mixed' (Natural & Cultural) UNESCO World Heritage Site.

national_parks.name: Valley of Flowers National Park
national_parks.key_fact: Known for its endemic alpine flowers; completely covered in snow during winter and only opens in summer.

national_parks.name: Dachigam National Park
national_parks.key_fact: The only area in the world where the critically endangered Hangul is found.
